_comment: SMAC-style tech tree structure (owner directive 2026-07-27, researched against Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri: categories form an INTERTWINING tree; every tech has AT MOST TWO prerequisites; tiers flow foundations -> frontier; blind research means the far tree is fog). Three branches for now (owner: 'just 3 pages for the moment'). RULES: roots are the FINITE set of already-built capabilities — curated at the CAPABILITY level, deliberately not a per-RB retrofit; techs reference either a backlog row (ref: RB-*, state read LIVE from RESEARCH_BACKLOG's state column — that file stays the single state source for RB items) or are curated near-frontier items (allowed state: available only; completion later lands in the ledger/backlog and promotes the node). Every tech's prereqs list existing root/tech ids and is capped at 2, per SMAC; edges are design statements about what COMBINES into what. Colors validated 2026-07-27 with the dataviz palette validator on the dark surface (all four checks pass; gold-green tritan dE 9.9 sits in the legal-with-secondary-encoding band, and every node carries its branch icon + text label, never color alone).

techs.title: Tech Tree App Review
techs.research: review the tech-tree system itself and generate improvement items across GUI, data model, interactivity, automation, progress tie-ins and self-testing
prelim: OWNER-APPROVED SCOPE (2026-07-28, all six): the review generates improvement ITEMS — new tech nodes, spec edits, and small direct fixes — across the six categories below, RANKED by value-per-effort. It ships the top slice, not the whole list; unshipped items become named techs or fog seeds so nothing evaporates.

1 · GUI/UX: a real drawn tree — SVG edges connecting nodes instead of tier columns; per-tech datalinks pages (one page per tech, unlimited Preliminary Data); hover/detail states; mobile layout; motion when a node changes tier. The current tier-column layout was v1 pragmatism, not a decision.

2 · Data model & rules: SMAC-style tiers/levels; 'what this unlocks' effects per tech; flavor quotes (original ones); effort/value estimates; TYPED edges — the owner's own verbs 'combining / extending / improving' are three different relationships currently flattened into one 'combines' chip; per-node revision history with provenance.

3 · Interactivity & signals: a request button on EVERY available tech, not just review nodes; an idea box on fog nodes so the owner can type a suggestion straight into the signal queue from the page (fog → named tech without a chat turn); a signal-history view rendering the append-only queue.

4 · Automation & write-back: the review operation itself producing tech-tree.json edits with provenance notes; an auto-promotion path for curated techs when their work completes (RB-refs already promote themselves via backlog state; curated nodes need manual edits today); a tech-tree-schema orient probe so a malformed spec cannot ship — the builder throws at render time, but a probe catches it at orient.

5 · Progress-picture tie-in: per-branch research counts (or the frontier itself) rendered into the committed progress.svg so the lanes and the tree tell one story — via committed inputs only, preserving the byte-compare staleness guarantee; grown nodes linking to the ledger cycle that researched them.

6 · App self-testing: extend the live browser harness to the three tech pages — nothing currently clicks a signal button or opens a Preliminary Data block in a real browser; the check must ack its own test click as a test click (the c139 rule) so the queue stays honest.
Constraint carried from the tree's own rules: every improvement item the review proposes must name its ≤2 foundations before it leaves the fog — the review is subject to the discipline it audits.

techs.title: Tech Tree & Project Review
techs.research: review the project plans and the tree itself; improve, and where needed create, the ideas for upcoming research
prelim: Scope of a review pass: every open/partial backlog row, every tech node on this tree, the roadmap steps, and the fog slots. The output is not a report — it is EDITS: sharpened research texts, corrected prereq edges, new tech nodes, and (rarely) a retired one, each traceable to a reason.

Idea quality has a measurable proxy here: a research text is good when it names the REMAINDER (what to build next), not the answered question — the c129 rule. A review should rewrite any node whose text a newcomer could not act on tomorrow.

Sources to mine for NEW tech ideas, in order of signal strength: (1) the ledger's second_order slugs — every earned rule implies a tool that enforces it; (2) defects caught post-ship — each is a missing check wanting to become a node; (3) owed[] items that recur; (4) branch imbalance — a branch whose available list runs dry needs ideation before it needs code.
Prereq edges are claims, and reviews should re-verify them: does TECH-DASH2B still genuinely combine CR-ENGINE + TR-PAGE, or has the design drifted? An edge nobody believes is worse than no edge.

Fog promotion is the creative act: a Future Technology slot becomes a named tech when two foundations suggest a combination nobody has written down. Candidate seeds noticed so far: probe results rendered onto the tree nodes themselves (TR-PROBES + TR-PAGE); a crawl-quality scoreboard fed by content intelligence (CR-INTEL + TR-PICTURE); signal-driven research queues generalised beyond this one button (this very node + TR-PROMPT).
Anti-goal: the review must not inflate the tree. SMAC's discipline applies to ideation too — a node that cannot name its two foundations is not ready to leave the fog.

techs.title: Staged-Divergence Proof
techs.research: harness base-URL mode + the staged SSR-vs-API divergence that gives L3 observed proof
prelim: The gap being closed: L3 (DOM agrees with live API) is reasoned, not observed — a freshly spawned server renders current SSR, so DOM and API agree by construction. The proof needs data to MOVE after boot.

Sketch: start the server against a fixture ledger, load the page once, append a stanza to the fixture, reload WITHOUT restarting — assert the DOM shows the new count while a frozen page would show the old one. Run it both with and without the c128.5 refresh() line to see the assertion flip.
